label: Movies
rubric: Critical acclaim · Genre/cultural influence · Rewatchability & fan devotion · Commercial performance

entries.name: The Godfather
entries.rationale: The benchmark against which American cinema is still measured.

entries.name: Parasite
entries.rationale: First non-English Best Picture winner and a genre-bending critical phenomenon.

entries.name: Pulp Fiction
entries.rationale: Reshaped independent film structure and dialogue for a generation.

entries.name: The Dark Knight
entries.rationale: Elevated the comic book film into serious dramatic territory.

entries.name: The Shawshank Redemption
entries.rationale: Perennially topping audience-voted lists decades after a soft opening.

entries.name: Mad Max: Fury Road
entries.rationale: Six Oscars and near-universal acclaim as one of the best-made action films ever.

entries.name: Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse
entries.rationale: Redefined what mainstream animation could look like and won the Oscar for it.

entries.name: Goodfellas
entries.rationale: The template for modern crime filmmaking, endlessly imitated.

entries.name: Schindler's List
entries.rationale: Best Picture winner of enormous historical and emotional weight.

entries.name: Spirited Away
entries.rationale: The high-water mark for animation worldwide and an Oscar winner.

entries.name: Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back
entries.rationale: The sequel that proved franchise films could deepen rather than repeat.

entries.name: Casablanca
entries.rationale: The most quoted film in Hollywood history, still fully watchable.

entries.name: Get Out
entries.rationale: Genre-redefining social horror with an Oscar-winning original screenplay.

entries.name: The Matrix
entries.rationale: Changed action filmmaking visually and permanently entered the language.

entries.name: 2001: A Space Odyssey
entries.rationale: The foundational text for serious science fiction on film.

entries.name: Inception
entries.rationale: A rare blockbuster that was both commercially huge and intellectually ambitious.

entries.name: Alien
entries.rationale: Fused horror and sci-fi into a template still being copied.

entries.name: The Silence of the Lambs
entries.rationale: One of only three films to sweep the top five Oscar categories.

entries.name: There Will Be Blood
entries.rationale: Widely cited as the defining American film of its decade.

entries.name: Forrest Gump
entries.rationale: Best Picture winner with enormous popular affection, though critically debated.

entries.name: Titanic
entries.rationale: Record-breaking commercial juggernaut and an eleven-Oscar sweep.

entries.name: La La Land
entries.rationale: Revived the movie musical with a record-tying nomination haul.

entries.name: Jaws
entries.rationale: Invented the summer blockbuster as a concept.

entries.name: No Country for Old Men
entries.rationale: Best Picture winner with one of cinema's great antagonists.

entries.name: Toy Story
entries.rationale: The first fully computer-animated feature and still a storytelling benchmark.

entries.name: Everything Everywhere All at Once
entries.rationale: Swept the major Oscars as an unlikely genre-mashing indie.

entries.name: Oppenheimer
entries.rationale: Best Picture winner that turned a three-hour talk-heavy drama into a global event.

entries.name: Jurassic Park
entries.rationale: A special-effects landmark that still holds up remarkably well.

entries.name: Blade Runner 2049
entries.rationale: A visually stunning sequel that critics rate alongside the original.

entries.name: Back to the Future
entries.rationale: Near-perfect crowd-pleasing construction and endless rewatchability.

entries.name: Whiplash
entries.rationale: A small film with outsized intensity and lasting cultural staying power.

entries.name: Moonlight
entries.rationale: Best Picture winner of rare intimacy and craft.

entries.name: The Lion King
entries.rationale: The peak of the Disney Renaissance with an all-time soundtrack.

entries.name: Interstellar
entries.rationale: Ambitious hard sci-fi with a devoted and growing fanbase.

entries.name: The Departed
entries.rationale: Tightly wound crime thriller that finally won its director Best Director.

entries.name: The Grand Budapest Hotel
entries.rationale: The most complete expression of a singular visual style, with four Oscars.

entries.name: Gladiator
entries.rationale: Revived the historical epic and won Best Picture doing it.

entries.name: The Social Network
entries.rationale: Razor-sharp screenwriting that captured its era with unusual precision.

entries.name: Knives Out
entries.rationale: Modernized the whodunnit into a genuine crowd-pleaser and franchise.

entries.name: Fight Club
entries.rationale: A cult phenomenon with enormous staying power despite a divided initial reception.

entries.name: Dune
entries.rationale: Turned a famously unfilmable novel into a visual and commercial success.

entries.name: Django Unchained
entries.rationale: Bold, hugely entertaining, and an Oscar-winning original screenplay.

entries.name: Black Panther
entries.rationale: First superhero film nominated for Best Picture, with major cultural impact.

entries.name: Avengers: Endgame
entries.rationale: The biggest event-movie payoff ever staged, though light on critical prestige.

entries.name: Barbie
entries.rationale: A billion-dollar cultural moment with far more subtext than expected.

entries.name: Mean Girls
entries.rationale: Endlessly quotable and permanently embedded in pop culture, but modest in scope.

entries.name: Shrek
entries.rationale: Won the first Best Animated Feature Oscar and became a meme institution.

entries.name: Deadpool
entries.rationale: Proved R-rated superhero comedy could be enormous, though critically lightweight.

entries.name: Superbad
entries.rationale: A defining teen comedy of its era with strong rewatch value, low prestige.

entries.name: The Hangover
entries.rationale: Massive commercial hit and comedy landmark, but the acclaim faded fast.
